articles.title: Pakistan abused us on Diwali, India U19 wanted to answer on field: Yashveer Goud - India Today
articles.summary: Pakistan abused us on Diwali, India U19 wanted to answer on field: Yashveer Goud India Today
articles.content: India U19 cricketer Yashveer Goud said the team's determination to respond to Pakistan's on-field taunts was a major motivation behind their celebrations after winning the U19 Asia Cup final. India had suffered a defeat to their arch-rivals on Diwali in the league stage, but got the perfect opportunity to turn the tables when the two sides met again in the title clash.Pakistan had beaten India by three wickets in a thrilling group-stage encounter. India posted 208, with Arjun Rajput scoring a century, but Pakistan chased down the target, courtesy of a match-winning hundred from Hamza Zaroor. The defeat left the Indian players disappointed, particularly after an exchange of words and abusive language during the contest.India, however, kept their response for the final. Speaking to Sports Today, Yashveer explained why the celebrations after the title triumph carried extra emotion.“We had lost the match on Diwali. There was some exchange of words between us, including abusive language. We couldn't say anything after losing that match. We were waiting for the final. We wanted to perform well and show what India is capable of,” Yashveer said.India eventually produced a remarkable comeback to beat Pakistan by one wicket in the final on November 14. Chasing 338, they were in deep trouble at 2528 before Manal Chauhan (47) and Mohit Ulva (49 not out) revived the chase. Ulva struck the winning boundary off the final delivery to seal a memorable victory.Yashveer was among the players who celebrated passionately after the finish, with his reaction towards the opposition also drawing attention. Asked about the celebrations and the differing opinions around them, he said the Indian players were simply responding to what they had experienced earlier.“We were doing the same thing they had done. They were silent, and we were silent too. We were wearing the Indian jersey. We were waiting for this moment. Everyone was emotional,” he added.KAVYA EYES INDIA GOALWhile much of the attention has been on India's title-winning performance and the players' emotional celebrations, the U19 Asia Cup has also provided a platform for young cricketers to showcase their potential. However, the challenge for players at this level is to carry that form forward and eventually earn a place in the senior team.Kavya Patel has taken a step in that direction, finishing the tournament with eight wickets. The youngster has set his sights on representing India at the senior level, following a pathway that several former U19 cricketers, including Virat Kohli, have successfully taken.For Kavya, though, the key is to remain patient, focus on the process and make the most of every opportunity rather than get carried away by the bigger ambition.“Yes, that is the main goal. But we have to follow the process step by step and focus on that. Whatever match we play, we have to give it our full intensity. If we do that, things will fall into place,” Kavya said.India's triumph also marked the end of a prolonged wait for the title. Having last won the U19 Asia Cup in 2021, India missed out on the final in 2023 after losing to Bangladesh in the semi-finals. They then suffered a 59-run defeat to Bangladesh in the 2024 final before going down to Pakistan by 191 runs in the 2025 summit clash.In 2026, India finally reclaimed the crown, beating Pakistan by one wicket in a last-ball thriller to win the U19 Asia Cup for the first time in three editions.- Ends

articles.title: Bangladesh, USA to host cricket qualifiers for 2028 Los Angeles Olympics - India Today
articles.summary: Bangladesh, USA to host cricket qualifiers for 2028 Los Angeles Olympics India Today
articles.content: Bangladesh and the United States will host the final qualifying tournaments for cricket's return to the Olympic Games at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced on Sunday, November 15.The men's qualifier will be held in Bangladesh from February 5 to 13, 2028, while the women's tournament will take place in the USA from February 26 to March 5. Both competitions will feature eight teams, with the winners securing the final qualification berths for the Olympic Games.Cricket will return to the Olympics after a gap of 128 years, having last featured at the 1900 Paris Games. The sport's inclusion in LA28 marks a significant milestone in its global growth, with both men's and women's T20 competitions set to be played in Los Angeles."The events constitute the final stage of the qualification pathway for cricket's return to the Olympic programme at LA28," the ICC said in a statement following its board meetings in Bali, Indonesia.Each qualifier will feature eight teams divided into two groups of four. Teams will play each other once in the group stage, with the two group winners advancing to the final. The winner of the summit clash will claim the last available Olympic spot.INDIA WOMEN ALREADY QUALIFIED FOR LA28Six nations will compete in each of the men's and women's T20 competitions at the Los Angeles Games, with Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania guaranteed representation.India's women's team has already secured qualification after emerging as the highest-placed Asian side at the Women's T20 World Cup earlier this year. Australia, South Africa and Great Britain have also booked their places through the continental qualification pathway.The Indian men's team is also well placed to make the cut. The men's qualification will be determined through the ICC T20I rankings as of December 31, 2026, with the highest-ranked eligible team from each of the four regions earning direct entry. The USA, as hosts, will also have an opportunity to qualify, subject to meeting the ICC's ranking criteria.Meanwhile, the ICC also confirmed qualification details for its upcoming global tournaments.The 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier, scheduled for February and March 2027, will feature 10 teams competing in 23 matches. The top four sides will progress to the World Cup in South Africa, with the winner advancing directly to the group stage.The 2028 Men's T20 World Cup Global Qualifier will feature 16 teams and 31 matches in the first quarter of 2028. Eight teams will earn qualification for the tournament, which will be hosted by Australia and New Zealand.- Ends

articles.title: Pakistan a soft target, India should show aggression against bigger teams: Manjrekar - India Today
articles.summary: Pakistan a soft target, India should show aggression against bigger teams: Manjrekar India Today
articles.content: Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar has questioned the aggressive celebrations of the Indian U-19 team following its dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Asia Cup final, suggesting that the youngsters should direct their aggression towards stronger opponents.India pulled off a remarkable last-ball victory to reclaim the Under-19 Asia Cup title in Oman on Saturday, November 14. However, the celebrations following the triumph did not go down well with Manjrekar, who took to social media to share his views.Describing Pakistan as a 'soft and easy target', the former India batter suggested that the Indian team should show the same aggression against Australia, South Africa, New Zealand and England."Indian cricket should now pick guys of their own size if they want to show 'aggression' on the field. Pak is now a soft & easy target. I suggest Aus, SA, NZ & Eng" Manjrekar posted on X. His remarks came after India produced a remarkable fightback to chase down Pakistan's imposing total of 337 for nine, sealing the contest with one wicket and one ball to spare.MOHIT ULVA LEADS INDIA'S REMARKABLE COMEBACKIndia's chase was far from straightforward, with Pakistan appearing to have the contest under control after reducing the defending champions to 252 for eight in the 42nd over.Earlier, captain Lakshya Raichandani scored 80 off 101 balls, while Aaryavir Sehwag contributed 58 as the opening pair added 95 runs. However, a flurry of wickets left India needing a special effort from the lower order.Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva provided exactly that, stitching together a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket. Manal scored 47 off just 32 deliveries before departing with India still needing 36 runs and only one wicket remaining.Mohit then found an able partner in No. 11 Chigurupati Venkata, who remained unbeaten on 11 off eight balls. With eight runs required in the final over, the equation came down to three runs from the last delivery.Facing leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain, Mohit smashed the final ball towards wide long-off for a boundary, triggering wild celebrations in the Indian camp. He remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls to complete one of the most memorable finishes of the tournament.India finished on 339 for nine to lift the title, but the celebrations that followed became the subject of Manjrekar's pointed criticism.- Ends

articles.contentMarathi: Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar has questioned the aggressive celebrations of the Indian U-19 team following its dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Asia Cup final, suggesting that the youngsters should direct their aggression towards stronger opponents.India pulled off a remarkable last-ball victory to reclaim the Under-19 Asia Cup title in Oman on Saturday, November 14. However, the celebrations following the triumph did not go down well with Manjrekar, who took to social media to share his views.Describing Pakistan as a 'soft and easy target', the former India batter suggested that the Indian team should show the same aggression against Australia, South Africa, New Zealand and England."Indian cricket should now pick guys of their own size if they want to show 'aggression' on the field. Pak is now a soft & easy target. I suggest Aus, SA, NZ & Eng" Manjrekar posted on X. His remarks came after India produced a remarkable fightback to chase down Pakistan's imposing total of 337 for nine, sealing the contest with one wicket and one ball to spare.MOHIT ULVA LEADS INDIA'S REMARKABLE COMEBACKIndia's chase was far from straightforward, with Pakistan appearing to have the contest under control after reducing the defending champions to 252 for eight in the 42nd over.Earlier, captain Lakshya Raichandani scored 80 off 101 balls, while Aaryavir Sehwag contributed 58 as the opening pair added 95 runs. However, a flurry of wickets left India needing a special effort from the lower order.Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva provided exactly that, stitching together a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket. Manal scored 47 off just 32 deliveries before departing with India still needing 36 runs and only one wicket remaining.Mohit then found an able partner in No. 11 Chigurupati Venkata, who remained unbeaten on 11 off eight balls. With eight runs required in the final over, the equation came down to three runs from the last delivery.Facing leg-spinner Ahmed Hussain, Mohit smashed the final ball towards wide long-off for a boundary, triggering wild celebrations in the Indian camp. He remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls to complete one of the most memorable finishes of the tournament.India finished on 339 for nine to lift the title, but the celebrations that followed became the subject of Manjrekar's pointed criticism.- Ends

articles.title: Telangana CM Reddy, Sports Minister Mandaviya unveil logo & mascot for Khelo India Youth Games - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Telangana CM Reddy, Sports Minister Mandaviya unveil logo & mascot for Khelo India Youth Games The New Indian Express
articles.content: NEW DELHI: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi to attend the eighth Khelo India Youth Games, scheduled in Telangana from December 11 to 22. Accompanied by Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, the Chief Minister met the Prime Minister before jointly unveiling the Games’ logo and mascot with the Union Sports Minister.Hosting the Games for the first time, Telangana will welcome around 8,000 athletes and participants across Hyderabad, Khammam, Karimnagar, Hanumakonda, Mahabubnagar and Nizamabad. The unveiling was attended by Telangana Ministers Vakiti Srihari and N Uttam Kumar Reddy; Sports Advisor and Telangana Olympic Association president A P Jithender Reddy; Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju; Union Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao; Joint Secretary Veenyl Krishna; Special Chief Secretary, Sports, Vani Prasad; Vice Chairman and Managing Director Sonibala Devi; and senior Union and state government officials.During the occasion, Revanth Reddy said: "Hosting the Khelo India Youth Games is a proud moment for Telangana. We are committed to giving young athletes the training, education and infrastructure they need to succeed. Taking the Games across six cities will inspire more youngsters to embrace sport. Our ambition is to nurture Olympic medallists and, one day, host the Olympic Games."Reddy thanked Mandaviya for the hosting opportunity and highlighted sport's role in advancing the Prime Minister’s vision of Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat, encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse.The mascot, ‘Neelamani’, embodies youthful energy, courage, agility and cultural pride. Its blue and turquoise feathers convey freedom and confidence, while its crest, eyes and beak represent momentum, focus and leadership.The logo combines sporting silhouettes with Telangana landmarks and cultural symbols, including the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, Hussain Sagar’s Buddha statue, the Tangedu flower and the proposed Gandhi Tower at Bapu Ghat. The tagline, "Khel Ka Junoon, Telangana Ki Jaan Aur Pehchaan," celebrates sport as part of the state's identity. The Games will feature 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events. Softball will make its competitive debut, while sailing and karra samu join as demonstration sports, expanding opportunities for young athletes to showcase their talent. .Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.content: CHENNAI BADMINTON Karnataka boys, Tamil Nadu girls crowned champions in 49th Junior Team Championships Karnataka boys and Tamil Nadu girls were crowned champions in the 49th Junior National Badminton Championships with comfortable 2-0 wins over their respective opponents. With both defending champions Mizoram boys and Telangana girls failing to qualify for the Inter-Zonals, the titles were up for grabs. In the finals, Karnataka defeated Assam 2-0 while Tamil Nadu girls got the better of last edition silver medallist Delhi 2-0. In the girls’ team final, 2025 Asian Under-17 girls singles champion Diksha SR gave Tamil Nadu a winning start as she defeated Rishika Nandi 15-12, 15-12. The women’s doubles combination of Ananya Arun and Anjana Manikandan then sealed the victory with a 16-14, 12-15, 15-10 lead over Nandi and Ishita Negi. The men’s singles final saw Hardik Divyansh defeat 2023 Asian U-15 champion Bornil Changmai. The formidable combination of Pavan and Punith Suresh then got the better of Changmai and Aanayan Borah 9-15, 15-10, 7-15 to clinch the crown. RESULTS Boys U-19: Karnataka bt Assam 2-0 (Hardik Divyansh bt Bornil Changmai 18-16, 15-6; Pavan Suresh/Punith Suresh bt Aanayan Borah/Changmai 15-9, 10-15, 15-7) Girls U-19: Tamil Nadu bt Delhi 2-0 (Diksha SR bt Rishika Nandi 15-12, 15-12; Ananya Arun/Anjana Manikandan bt Nandi/Ishita Negi 16-14, 12-15, 15-10) -Team Sportstar MOTORSPORTS Dramatic opening day of National Car Racing Championship The opening day of round 2 of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship was dramatic in nature, filled with late changes and overtakes. Augustine Boby edged Shatveer Shetty by a mere 0.032 seconds in the F1300 Novice Cup here on Sunday. Mehul Agarwal produced a late overtake to beat teammate Arya Singh by 0.237 seconds in LGB Formula 4, while Deepak Ravikumar staged a remarkable recovery from 15th after an early stall to win the second Indian Junior Touring Cars race by 0.308 seconds. Srinivas Teja had won the opening race in the category. In the other categories, Bengaluru’s Anish Shetty won the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup Pro race, while Vadodara’s Kabir Sahoch continued his winning run in the amateur class despite two red-flag interruptions at the Kari Motor Speedway. Mumbai’s Pratik Sonawane completed a double in the gentleman class of the JK Tyre Levitas Cup, while Arjun Narendran won the Indian Super Touring Cars race and Balaprasath A triumphed in Indian Touring Cars. Diljith T S also secured a double in Super Stock. The Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup amateur race witnessed further drama with a last-lap collision between Paramjeet Singh and Pushpendra Kumar Markandey, allowing Brandon Dsouza to climb from ninth on the grid to third. Action concludes on Sunday with the final day of round 2. -Team Sportstar MORE SPORTS Six cities across Telangana to host the Khelo India Youth Games 2026 The logo and mascot for the eighth edition of Khelo India Youth Games were unveiled on Sunday by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A Revanath Reddy. The tournament is going to be played across six cities in Telangana: Hyderabad, Khammam, Karimnagar, Hanumakonda, Mahabubnagar and Nizamabad, between December 11 and 22. Around 8000 athletes are expected to participate in the event. “The Union Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is committed to promoting sports. Various competitions, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of the younger generation in sports,” said Mandaviya. This time, the tournament will have 29 events, including two demonstration events: sailing and karra samu. The three-day championship, organised by Indian Chess School, witnessed keen competition among 387 players across six FIDE-rated categories in the Under-9, Under-13 and Under-17 Open and Girls sections. In the Under-9 Open category, Veer Dhaval Shah (1501) of Jamnabai Narsee School, JVPD, emerged as the undisputed champion with a perfect score of seven points from seven rounds. Ivaan Dubey (1545), who had earlier won the Under-7 Open title in the first stage, secured second place with six points, while Aarav Ravi Jhavar (1571) of Jamnabai Narsee School finished third with six points. The Under-9 Girls category witnessed an exciting three-way finish, with Lavanya Singh (1448) of Sanjivani International School emerging champion with six points on superior tie-break. Ishi Singh (1538) of J. B. Petit High School for Girls also scored six points to secure second place, while Nikita Sandeep (1411) finished third with six points. In the Under-13 Open category, Vihaan Anupam Agrawal (1858) of Narayana Olympiad School emerged champion with six points from seven rounds, edging out top seed Nirvaan Nirav Shah (1956) of Don Bosco International School, who also scored six points but had to settle for second place on tie-break. In the Under-13 Girls category, Tisyaa Apurva Patt (1524) of Avalon Heights International School produced an impressive performance to clinch the championship with six points from seven rounds. Pranitha Bhava (1655) of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan Vidyalaya secured second place with 5.5 points. The Under-17 Open category witnessed a commanding performance by top seed AIM Hriday Maniar (1910), who maintained his winning streak throughout the championship to secure the title with a perfect score of seven points from seven rounds. Shaurya Ashish Modi (1626) finished second with 5.5 points, while Soham Sudarshan Sahamate (1667) secured third place, also with 5.5 points. In the Under-17 Girls category, top seed Drishya Naik (1713) emerged as a convincing champion with 6.5 points from seven rounds, finishing 1.5 points ahead of her nearest challengers. The championship served as the selection tournament for the National Schools Chess Championship, scheduled to be held in Ahmedabad from December 16 to 20, 2026. The top two finishers in each of the six categories have earned the opportunity to represent Maharashtra at the national championship. -Team Sportstar RESULTS Boys U-19: Karnataka bt Assam 2-0 (Hardik Divyansh bt Bornil Changmai 18-16, 15-6; Pavan Suresh/Punith Suresh bt Aanayan Borah/Changmai 15-9, 10-15, 15-7) Girls U-19: Tamil Nadu bt Delhi 2-0 (Diksha SR bt Rishika Nandi 15-12, 15-12; Ananya Arun/Anjana Manikandan bt Nandi/Ishita Negi 16-14, 12-15, 15-10)

articles.content: Mumbai The Maharashtra government’s Relief and Rehabilitation Department on Saturday (November 14) urged drought-affected farmers across the State to complete their e-KYC verification and obtain Farmer IDs at the earliest to ensure they can access financial assistance and benefits under various Central and State government schemes. According to the department, completing the necessary registration and verification procedures is essential for eligible beneficiaries to receive funds directly in their bank accounts. In a statement, the department said farmers must ensure that their information is updated on the AgriStack platform, which maintains updated farmer information and facilitates the delivery of benefits under agricultural and other government welfare schemes. It added that completing e-KYC verification and obtaining a Farmer ID would help minimise difficulties in accessing assistance and facilitate the timely transfer of benefits to eligible farmers. The State government also assured farmers that necessary assistance would be provided to resolve technical or other difficulties encountered during registration and verification. Farmers facing such issues have been advised to contact the relevant authorities rather than leave their applications incomplete. To obtain a Farmer ID, farmers have been asked to visit their nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with their Aadhaar card and Aadhaar-linked mobile number to complete the registration process. The department reiterated that updating farmer records and completing verification procedures were important to ensure the timely and transparent distribution of government benefits. It urged farmers across Maharashtra, particularly those affected by drought, to prioritise the process and complete the required formalities without delay.

articles.title: Australia and India strengthen sports partnership in Tamil Nadu - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Australia and India strengthen sports partnership in Tamil Nadu The New Indian Express
articles.content: CHENNAI: Building on the Australia-India Roadmap for Sports Collaboration, which was announced earlier this year in July, the Australian Consulate-General, Chennai welcomed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Basketball Australia and the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), marking a significant step forward in sports cooperation between the two nations. The MoU, which was signed on Friday, establishes a framework for collaboration in coach, player and referee development, high-performance sport, governance, sports integrity, and community engagement. Under the agreement, the two organisations will work together to create development pathways for athletes, coaches and officials, facilitate knowledge exchange, promote friendly competitions and exposure visits, and strengthen diaspora engagement.Aadhav Arjuna, president of the BFI, and Matt Scriven, Chief Executive Officer of Basketball Australia, formalised the partnership on behalf of their respective organisations. Matt Scriven said, "We are proud to announce this partnership with the Basketball Federation of India and to support basketball's rapid growth in one of the world's most exciting emerging basketball markets." Aadhav Arjuna said, "Basketball has a unique power to unite societies, transcend cultures and bring communities together. This partnership between Basketball Australia and the Basketball Federation of India is more than an MOU; it is a shared commitment to strengthening India's basketball ecosystem, nurturing future generations and building a pathway towards making India a basketball powerhouse in Asia and, one day, on the world stage. May the dribble become the heartbeat of every aspiring Indian basketball player, and the dream of representing India a reality." Witnessing the virtual MoU signing, Australian Consul-General in Chennai, Silai Zaki said, "Today's MoU reflects the growing momentum in the Australia-India sporting relationship. With the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad and the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games on the horizon, there has never been a better time for Australia and India to team up and build stronger sporting links." The growing sports partnership between Australia and India will be on full display in Chennai this December. On December 12, the opening match of the Men's Big Bash League (BBL) will be played at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, marking the first time a regular-season BBL match is being played outside Australia.During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Australia in July 2026, the two Prime Ministers had announced the Australia-India Roadmap for Sports Collaboration. .Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.title: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030 - The Hindu
articles.summary: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030 The Hindu
articles.content: Bengaluru KPMG in India opened its Sports Technology Hub, a platform designed to help sports organisations in the country accelerate digital transformation, unlock new growth opportunities and build future-ready sporting ecosystems. The initiative is expected to bring together emerging technologies, industry expertise, and practical use cases to address evolving business and operational challenges in the sports industry. As the sports industry continued to evolve, organisations were increasingly leveraging technology to enhance fan experiences, improve athlete performance and strengthen commercial outcomes, KPMG officials said, adding, ``However, fragmented data, legacy infrastructure, operational inefficiencies and rising expectations for personalised experiences continue to hinder innovation.’’ The Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru aims to address these challenges through practical solutions that sports organisations can evaluate and adopt. The hub was officially inaugurated by Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India, and P. T. Usha, President of the Indian Olympic Association, here on Friday. Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India, said, “Realising India’s potential in sports calls for innovation across the entire sports value chain. Our sports technology hub aims to bring industry expertise and technology together to help reshape how a sport is played, managed and experienced. As India strengthens its position on the global sports stage, technology will be central to building a more competitive, connected and future-ready sports ecosystem.” According to Prasanth Shanthakumaran, Partner and Head of Sports Sector, KPMG in India said, the hub showcases a range of technology-driven solutions, including AI-powered fan engagement platforms, smart stadium and venue management, athlete performance analytics, computer vision-based training and match insights, digital ticketing and loyalty solutions, and sponsorship measurement tools. It also incorporates capabilities in predictive maintenance, cybersecurity, sustainability and generative AI-enabled content creation to help sports organisations optimise operations and unlock new commercial opportunities. “The Sports Technology Hub brings together cutting-edge technologies such as AI, advanced analytics, computer vision, and digital platforms to address some of the most pressing challenges facing the sports industry today,’’ added Mr. Shanthakumaran. By showcasing practical, outcome-driven solutions, we aim to help sports organisations innovate faster, improve performance, and create more engaging experiences for fans, athletes, and partners, he further said. Designed as a collaborative platform, the Sports Technology Hub is expected to bring together sports federations, leagues, clubs, technology providers, startups and other industry stakeholders to explore and scale innovative solutions.
